answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a bridge as the anchor of the cost. A marble stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a quartz holds the reputation that makes it all...
